attribution.note: Marcus's own sentence in his own essay. It is not a quotation of Javorsky.

semantics.note: An unhedged retrospective observation. 'So far' is kept, and 'change all that' is fairly rendered as cancer's toll.

contract.note: The plain reading (no material reduction in cancer deaths or suffering) fits the bereavement context and is ordinary. The result still depends on whether limited clinical benefits count.

evidence.note: SHIELD-RT found fewer acute-care visits among ML-selected patients. But the trial randomised extra visits, not AI selection, so the benefit is not isolated to AI.
MASAI found fewer interval cancers with AI screening before the post. That is a screening outcome, not a demonstrated reduction in deaths or suffering.
Official figures on the continuing cancer burden. They do not show the counterfactual without AI.

reviews.rationale: No item shows a material reduction in cancer deaths or suffering that can be attributed to AI. SHIELD-RT and MASAI suggest some benefit but do not isolate AI or measure mortality. Equally, nothing establishes that there was no benefit, and continued deaths cannot prove it. Neither the support nor the contradiction condition is met.

attribution.note: Marcus's own sentence. The Ricks quote that comes just before it is separate.

semantics.note: A recurring pattern plus a causal explanation (poor understanding of biology). Rendered faithfully, with 'over and over' kept.

contract.note: Requiring candidate-level AI records of animal efficacy followed by human safety failure tracks his words. Excluding efficacy-only failures is a fair reading of 'not safely enough'.

evidence.note: Company disclosure: BEN-2293 was safe but missed its efficacy endpoints. One candidate cannot confirm or refute a recurring pattern.
Rentosertib was judged safe and well tolerated, with some discontinuations. This is not a development failure for safety reasons, and one success cannot disprove recurrence.
Company release that dates the rentosertib trial and describes the AI involvement. It does not bear on the claimed pattern.

reviews.rationale: The packet documents no AI-discovered candidate that showed animal efficacy and then failed in humans on safety, and nothing on the biological cause. The cited safe candidates cannot rule out repeated failures elsewhere. The evidence settles neither condition.

attribution.note: Marcus's own sentence. He endorses Javorsky's argument and adds his own AI prerequisite.

semantics.note: An unhedged forward-looking claim of necessity about what beating cancer will need. Read as causal or forecast, it is faithful and has no deadline.

contract.note: Testing necessity only once cancer is comprehensively controlled is fair to the words. The reading of 'beating cancer' as comprehensive, durable control is ordinary.

evidence.note: Official mortality data show cancer is not beaten. They do not test whether the named changes are necessary.

reviews.rationale: No deadline was given, and no documented comprehensive cancer control exists that would trigger the early-resolution rule. The prerequisites therefore cannot yet be tested, and the claim stays unresolved.
